dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats every 0.533 days, which is the same as the star's own starspot rotation period, and the star shows a very strong ~9000 ppm brightness swing at that period. The dip depth also grows from ~12300 to ~16300 ppm across sectors while on the same instrument. Together this is best explained by evolving starspots rather than a transiting Neptune-sized planet. No secondary eclipse or odd-even difference is seen, but the period and variability match the star.

reasons.why: Dip period is essentially identical to the star's spot period (1.00x) with extremely significant ~24235 ppm variability. That makes a spot modulation / variability harmonic the best explanation, not a transiting planet.
Very large (~9037 ppm, 55% of transit depth) out-of-dip swing with huge chi2 indicates strong spot-induced phase curve, not a flat planetary phase curve.
Depth increases systematically from 12319 to 16317 ppm across sectors on one light-curve source, exactly expected if the apparent dip depth tracks evolving spot coverage rather than a stable planet.
reasons.value: p_constant=0.00001961, depth_change_pct=28.27, depths 12319 to 16317 ppm; sector_depths_by_source verdict=changes_within_a_source

reasons.why: Duration 1.75x longer than central for this 0.427 Rsun M dwarf is well beyond planetary expectations (fit_b=1.835e-8) and also inconsistent with the stellar-radius based planet size, favouring an active variability interpretation over a planet.

Flat bottom and on-target centroid mimic a transit but flat-bottomed stellar eclipses and spot dips also appear flat; planet-like shape does not outweigh period=rotation + large phase curve in this active K/M dwarf.
